trigger: spellResisted with freeze: true — engine/combat.js#freezeFoe (a Freeze that hit, from the hero, a scroll or a Joiner)
after: Viper resists the freeze: the damage lands, the ice doesn't. 7 vs 12–20 (intel 5).
why: User ruling 2026-09-28: "if it hits and resists, deal damage, but no freeze." A Freeze rolls its resist only after the hit's damage lands, so its resist line can no longer say "no effect": it says the damage landed and only the ice was shrugged off, then the roll.

after: Viper resists the freeze: the damage lands, the ice doesn't
why: User ruling 2026-09-28: the rail twin of the Oracle line. A resisted Freeze still did its damage, so the rail must not read "no effect".

trigger: controlHeld with freeze: true — engine/combat.js#holdFoe via freezeFoe (a landed Freeze or the Birch Staff)
after: Viper is frozen for 3 rounds. Ice now, grudge later.
why: User ruling 2026-09-28: "freeze should never kill outright. It should deal its damage and freeze an enemy for 1d4 rounds." A Freeze now holds for its rolled d4 at every depth, so the line states the rounds plainly (never "not forever", which was the past-floor-12 hold's wording), then the joke.

trigger: controlHeld with freeze: true — engine/combat.js#holdFoe via freezeFoe
why: User ruling 2026-09-28: the rail says "frozen for N rounds". On the hero's own cast the rail folds the hit, a failed resist and this hold into one line ("Freeze hits Viper (4), frozen for 3 rounds"), so the damage and the rounds read together.

before: Viper's Heal — Viper frozen solid. It will keep.
why: User ruling 2026-09-28: a Joiner's Freeze never freezes a foe solid any more. Its hit reads as damage ("Viper's Freeze hits Viper for 6 hp."), and the d4 hold that follows is its own controlHeld line, so the frozen-solid branch is retired.

before: Viper casts Heal — Viper frozen solid
why: User ruling 2026-09-28: the rail twin. A Joiner's Freeze reads its damage ("Viper casts Freeze — Viper (6)"), and the hold is its own "frozen for N rounds" line; the frozen-solid branch is gone.

before: freezes up to 2 squares of opponents indefinitely; past floor 12, indefinitely means three rounds
after: freezes up to 2 squares of opponents for d4 rounds apiece, unless they resist; then they are just cold and angry
why: User rulings 2026-09-28: the Birch Staff's freeze follows the Freeze spell, a d4-round freeze on each foe it reaches unless that foe resists, at every depth. "Indefinitely" is no longer true anywhere, so the text states the d4 and the resist, then echoes Freeze's own "just cold and angry".
